title: Knowledge check: Middleware Ordering and Composition

questions.prompt: In Middleware Ordering and Composition, which statement best describes Request parsing before request-data consumers?
options: Connect this syllabus point to Middleware Ordering and Composition: state the expected behavior, identify a realistic edge case, and choose a test or observation that proves the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.
Log structured request IDs, outcomes, durations and safe diagnostic context. Redact secrets and personal data, then use actual error/latency trends to guide debugging.
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
questions.answer_key: Connect this syllabus point to Middleware Ordering and Composition: state the expected behavior, identify a realistic edge case, and choose a test or observation that proves the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.
questions.explanation: Connect this syllabus point to Middleware Ordering and Composition: state the expected behavior, identify a realistic edge case, and choose a test or observation that proves the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Middleware Ordering and Composition?
options: Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

Middleware executes in registration order. Each function should either complete the response, pass control, or forward an error; keep middleware responsibilities small and place parsing, security, routes, fallback, and error handlers intentionally.
questions.answer_key: Middleware executes in registration order. Each function should either complete the response, pass control, or forward an error; keep middleware responsibilities small and place parsing, security, routes, fallback, and error handlers intentionally.
questions.explanation: Middleware executes in registration order. Each function should either complete the response, pass control, or forward an error; keep middleware responsibilities small and place parsing, security, routes, fallback, and error handlers intentionally.

questions.prompt: A change related to Middleware Ordering and Composition appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
